expectations.text: The mass email with the rate card is cancelled; the increase is communicated privately to each returning sponsor at its debrief call, before the prospectus is public on Dec 1
expectations.evidence: 'unschedule the Monday email'; 'Seven 30-minute calls'; 'You're hearing this before the prospectus goes public.'

expectations.text: The sponsor-price increase is not set equal to the venue's 18%; the increase is derived from the venue line's share of the budget, stated as 'the venue raised its rate; sponsorship covers [share] of that cost'
expectations.evidence: 'The venue's 18% is a cost line, not the sponsor price'; 'sponsorship covers [share] of that cost'.

expectations.text: The new list price is attributed to the sponsor-pricing decision; until it exists, the price is quoted as indicative with a confirmation date
expectations.evidence: 'Price decision from event-sponsor-pricing'; 'Until pricing confirms, quote the new price as indicative.'

expectations.text: A published price-change date is set at least 30 days after Dec 1 (no earlier than Dec 31), with anyone signing before it paying the current price
expectations.evidence: 'no earlier than Dec 31'; 'Everyone who signs before it pays the current price, new sponsors included.'

expectations.text: The proposal that returning sponsors who sign before Dec 1 keep the old price is rejected as a returning-only discount by calendar
expectations.evidence: 'This is a returning-sponsor loyalty discount... returning-only discount by calendar.'

expectations.text: The advantage given to returning sponsors is hearing the price-change date first and privately, not a different price
expectations.evidence: 'Returning sponsors hear it first, privately. That head start is the advantage, not a different price.'

expectations.text: Tarnwick is called the same day the 'no' is read, enters the rescue path, and hears about the price increase only after its reason is known and answered
expectations.evidence: 'call today or tomorrow'; 'Don't mention the increase on the first call'.

expectations.text: Oakhaven's formal ask is scheduled before its Dec 15 budget lock, with the published price-change date covering the gap below the 90-day notice practitioners ask for
expectations.evidence: 'send it by about Dec 1'; 'The published price-change date covers the gap.'

expectations.text: The fix from each report's what-went-wrong section is placed in the same message as the price, ahead of the price
expectations.evidence: Email template puts 'What changes for you: [the fix from the report]' before 'Price:'. On the call the report walk-through comes before the price.

expectations.text: The increase is never justified on tenure or loyalty; it is tied to the documented venue change
expectations.evidence: The reason is 'The venue raised its rate; sponsorship covers [share]'.

expectations.text: The formal-ask email carries the clause that the current price applies to agreements signed before the published price-change date, because of the documented reason
expectations.evidence: 'The current price applies to agreements signed before [price-change date], because [venue cost line...]'.

expectations.text: Net revenue retention for this cohort is to be reported a second time at constant prices, so the 18% increase does not pass for growth
expectations.evidence: 'Report net retention a second time at constant prices, so the increase doesn't pass for growth.'
